title: AI-Run Modern LaTeX Manuscript Workflow and Replication Packet
description:
Compact workflow and replication record for the Modern LaTeX Editions of Mathematics Manuscripts project. It documents the AI-run scan-to-TeX-to-translation-to-audit-to-publication workflow, including local source acquisition, OCR/math-OCR witness generation, source-image slicing, high-DPI object crops, TeX compilation, web review handoffs, GitHub mirroring, and Zenodo publication.

Latest update, 2026-06-24. Adds source-witness/public-surface and archive-scope guardrail addenda from current SGA, Noether, Gordan, Steinitz, Deligne, Cayley, and local sweep maintenance lessons. The addenda formalize the difference between OCR/source-witness aids, working drafts, source-witnessed tranches, source-closed loci, critical editions, and unrelated local mathematical files that should not be published as part of this project.

Scope guardrail. Local sweep may inspect broad folders, but publication is limited to the manuscript transcription/translation/source-audit project unless Floris explicitly requests a named non-project upload. A file being mathematical, interesting, recently downloaded, or technically publishable is not enough.

Workflow status. The record is a reusable workflow packet, not a claim that any particular mathematical edition is critically complete. OCR, VLM, detector, crop, candidate-TeX, derivative PDF, and source-inventory outputs are witness and locator layers unless a source-specific audit promotes them. Source scans and source-object witnesses remain authority for transcription claims.

Corrections and contributions. Workflow corrections, tool notes, reproducibility improvements, and issue reports can be suggested through the GitHub mirror via issues or pull requests: https://github.com/KokunoYumeto/modern-latex-manuscripts.
notes: Adds workflow_addendum_20260624_source_witness_public_surface.md, workflow_addendum_20260624_archive_scope_guardrail.md, and the compact archive-scope guardrail ZIP. Core rules: do not let filenames carry quality claims; OCR is a coverage/source locator, not authority; high-resolution source packets should include page maps, object inventories, crops with context, output renders, stable object IDs, and ledger verdicts; audit bundles should be routed as provenance/support unless they close a public-facing uncertainty; found-on-disk does not mean publish; unrelated third-party TeX, new research drafts, Reddit downloads, Lean experiments, and personal/novel math files stay out unless Floris explicitly names the exact item for upload; critical-edition language is reserved for explicit human certification.
